bib.title: Unified Pre-training for Program Understanding and Generation

read.skipped: References and qualitative code figures skimmed

question: Can one denoising seq2seq model pre-trained on code and related natural language support both program understanding and generation tasks?
hypothesis: Denoising pre-training on unlabeled Java, Python and StackOverflow text lets a model learn program syntax and semantics that transfer to generation and classification tasks, even with few labels.
contributions: PLBART, a BART-base-sized seq2seq model pre-trained on Java, Python and NL
Evaluation on summarization, generation, translation, repair, clone and vulnerability detection
Analysis that it learns syntax, style and data flow and works with limited annotations

method.summary: BART-base architecture pre-trained with denoising (masking, deletion, span infilling) on Java and Python functions from GitHub plus StackOverflow posts, then fine-tuned per task on CodeXGLUE datasets.
method.task: denoising seq2seq pre-training for code; fine-tuned for summarization, generation, translation, repair, classification

datasets.name: GitHub Java functions
datasets.size: 352 GB; 36.4 B tokens (all-language row); 470 M documents (functions)
datasets.source: Google BigQuery GitHub repos; pipeline of Lachaux et al. 2020
datasets.preprocessing: function extraction following Lachaux et al. 2020

datasets.name: StackOverflow posts (NL)
datasets.preprocessing: questions and answers kept, code snippets excluded

models.name: PLBART
models.architecture: BART-base seq2seq transformer plus extra layer-norm on encoder and decoder top (stabilises FP16)
models.init_from: inferred: random init (pre-trained from scratch on the corpus)
models.tokenizer: sentencepiece learned on 1/5 of pretraining data
models.context: 512 pretraining max length; n_positions 1024 in Table 10

models.name: RoBERTa / RoBERTa (code) / CodeBERT / GraphCodeBERT / GPT-2 / CodeGPT-2 / CodeGPT-adapted
models.architecture: encoder-only with random decoder, or decoder-only

other.note: GraphCodeBERT numbers taken from its paper; baselines for summarization from Feng et al. 2020

training.objective: denoising autoencoding: maximize sum log P(x_j | f(x_j)); noise = token masking, token deletion, token infilling; 35% of tokens masked; span lengths Poisson (lambda=3.5)
training.precision: inferred: FP16, from extra layer-norm 'to stabilize training with FP16 precision'
training.dropout: 0.1, reduced to 0.05 at 50K steps and 0 at 80K steps

other.language_sampling: multinomial with alpha=0.3 smoothing (Conneau and Lample 2019); PL has 14x more data than NL
other.finetune: max 100K steps, 2500 warm-up, max lr 3e-5, effective batch 32, dropout 0.1, best checkpoint by validation BLEU or accuracy, one RTX 2080 Ti
other.finetune_table10: PLBART lr 5e-5, batch 32, Adam (Table 10 conflicts with 3e-5 in text)
other.classification: input fed to encoder and decoder; last decoder token representation to linear classifier

inference.prompting: fine-tuning format: source to encoder with language id appended, target prefixed with language id

metrics.name: smoothed BLEU-4
metrics.definition: smoothed n-gram overlap (Lin and Och 2004), summarization

metrics.name: corpus BLEU
metrics.definition: corpus-level n-gram overlap, other generation tasks

metrics.name: CodeBLEU
metrics.definition: BLEU plus AST and data-flow match (Ren et al. 2020)

metrics.name: accuracy / F1
metrics.definition: vulnerability detection accuracy; clone detection F1

eval.protocol: single reported number per cell; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated

availability.data: CodeXGLUE public splits; GitHub BigQuery and StackExchange dump

results.claim: PLBART beats CodeBERT on average smoothed BLEU-4 for code summarization over six languages
results.setup: CodeXGLUE/CodeSearchNet summarization, Ruby/JS/Go/Python/Java/PHP, fine-tuned PLBART; baselines from Feng et al. 2020

results.claim: Largest summarization gain is on Ruby (smallest training set), a language not in pretraining

Text-to-Java generation on CONCODE: PLBART best BLEU
CodeGPT-adapted has higher exact match than PLBART on CONCODE
With only 10K CONCODE fine-tuning examples PLBART still gets CodeBLEU above all baselines
results.note: Text says PLBART10K 'outperforms all baselines in terms of CodeBLEU', but CodeGPT-adapted has 35.98 > 33.32 in the table; true only against the other baselines.

limits: Pretrained only on Java, Python and English StackOverflow; PHP and Ruby, C#, C/C++ are unseen
Neither PLBART nor CodeBERT is state-of-the-art for vulnerability detection; graph models are better
Single-task fine-tuning only; joint fine-tuning left to future work
No seeds, variance or significance testing reported
Claims of learned syntax and data flow rest on a few qualitative examples and the small-data ablation
Fine-tuning learning rate stated as 3e-5 in text but 5e-5 in Table 10
Compared models differ in pretraining data and size; 2021 baselines now dated
